newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ SAYS PROPERTY TO OUTPERFORM IN 97/98.
newsitem.headline: ANZ SAYS PROPERTY TO OUTPERFORM IN 97/98.

text.p: The funds management arm of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Tuesday it expects the property market to provide the best returns over the next year as international share markets end their bull run.
"Over the year to June 30, 1998, direct property is expected to return an average of 10.8 percent, listed property trusts 8.6 percent and Australian shares 7.8 percent," ANZ Funds Management said,
The funds group said it forecast international shares and fixed interest investments would deliver lower returns than cash, yielding 5.3 percent and 3.4 percent respectively.
"Cash is expected to return 5.5 percent," the fund manager said in its latest quarterly returns survey.
ANZ Funds Management's chief investment officer, Glen Wooley said the lower nominal returns expected across all investment classes were a result of structurally lower inflation levels.
"In this new era of low inflation, and a dampened business cycle, the focus is on quality of earnings streams and providing better shareholder value," Wooley said in the survey.
Wooley said ANZ Funds Management's balanced portfolios have been underweight in international equities, particularly in the U.S., and overweight cash in anticipation of a market correction.
He said people investing in diversified or balanced funds could expect returns, on average, of around 6.4 percent over the year to June 30, 1998.

ANZ Funds Management publishes its Expected Returns Survey which polls the leading broking house strategists across Australia to measure expected market returns for all investment sectors each quarter.
